tasks.name: Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies.

topics.name: AI, ML, Deep Learning & Neural Network Concepts
Batch, Real-Time, Asynchronous & Serverless Inferencing
Data Types: Tabular, Time-Series, Image, Text, Structured vs Unstructured
Supervised, Unsupervised & Reinforcement Learning

selection_rules: Select supervised learning when labeled ground-truth targets exist; choose unsupervised learning for clustering and pattern discovery without labels.
Choose real-time inferencing for interactive millisecond responses; choose batch inferencing for scheduled high-throughput offline processing.
Distinguish deep learning neural networks from classical ML algorithms based on autonomous representation learning and massive data scaling.
common_confusions: Confusing real-time inference endpoints with asynchronous or batch transform jobs.
Assuming reinforcement learning is supervised because it uses feedback and rewards.
Confusing labeled structured tabular data with unstructured multimodal inputs.

tasks.name: Identify practical use cases for AI.

topics.name: AI Value Proposition, Decision Support & Scalability
When AI Is Not Appropriate & Deterministic Alternatives
Technique Selection: Regression, Classification, Clustering
AWS Managed AI Services (Transcribe, Translate, Comprehend, Lex, Polly)
Traditional ML vs Foundation Models Selection Criteria

selection_rules: Use deterministic rule-based algorithms rather than ML when exact, auditable mathematical logic without variance is required.
Prefer pre-trained AWS managed AI services (Comprehend, Transcribe, Polly) over custom models when standard NLP/audio tasks meet requirements.
Choose classification for discrete categorical prediction, regression for continuous numerical values, and clustering for grouping unlabelled records.
common_confusions: Using an expensive generative LLM where a lightweight classification model or deterministic rule solves the problem.
Confusing Amazon Lex conversational bots with Amazon Polly text-to-speech synthesis.
Attempting to train custom models when managed pre-trained APIs already provide turn-key capabilities.

tasks.name: Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle.

topics.name: AI/ML Pipeline: Data Prep, Training, Tuning, Inference
Foundation Model Sourcing: Pre-trained, Custom, Open Source
Production Deployment: Managed APIs vs Self-Hosted Endpoints
MLOps: Experiment Tracking, CI/CD, Model Monitoring & Retraining
Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 & Business ROI

selection_rules: Optimize for precision when false positives are costly (e.g., fraud prevention); optimize for recall when false negatives are critical (e.g., security threat detection).
Implement continuous model monitoring to detect data drift and concept drift before degrading production inferences.
Prefer managed API endpoints (SageMaker Serverless / Bedrock APIs) to reduce operational burden for intermittent workloads.
common_confusions: Assuming high accuracy alone guarantees model quality on imbalanced datasets without checking precision and recall.
Treating ML deployment as a one-time release rather than a monitored, recurring MLOps lifecycle.
Confusing data drift (input distribution shifts) with concept drift (target relationship shifts).

tasks.name: Explain the basic concepts of generative AI (GenAI).

topics.name: Tokens, Embeddings, Vectors & Transformer Architectures
Diffusion Models & Multimodal Generation (Text, Image, Audio, Video)
Foundation Model Lifecycle: Data Selection, Pre-training, Fine-tuning, Deployment
Token-Based Pricing, Context Windows & Inference Economics
Agentic AI Concepts: Tool Usage, MCP, Orchestration & Memory

selection_rules: Account for prompt and generation token counts when projecting inference costs and model context window constraints.
Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) or tool-calling frameworks to connect generative agents safely to external databases and APIs.
Recognize that pre-training foundation models from scratch is rarely justified; adapt existing models via prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning.
common_confusions: Confusing tokens with raw words or character counts (1 token ≈ 0.75 words in English).
Assuming foundation models store facts as relational databases rather than probabilistic associative weights.
Confusing single-turn conversational prompting with multi-agent tool-augmented workflows.

tasks.name: Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems.

topics.name: GenAI Strengths: Content Synthesis, Conversational Agility & Code Generation
GenAI Risks: Hallucinations, Nondeterminism & Interpretability
Selection Factors: Latency, Modality, Model Complexity & Cost
Business Alignment Metrics: ROI, Task Completion Rate & Efficiency

selection_rules: Implement grounding techniques (RAG, guardrails, retrieval verification) when factual veracity is critical to mitigate hallucination.
Set temperature close to 0 for deterministic, analytical outputs; use higher temperature for creative brainstorming.
Balance model parameter scale against latency and cost budgets based on task difficulty.
common_confusions: Treating generative model outputs as deterministic facts without verification.
Assuming larger models are always superior regardless of response latency and token costs.
Ignoring nondeterminism in automated workflows that require reproducible outputs.

tasks.name: Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications.

topics.name: Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker AI & SageMaker JumpStart Ecosystem
AWS Specialized Hardware: Trainium, Inferentia & GPU Instances
Managed Bedrock vs Self-Hosted SageMaker Trade-offs
Amazon Bedrock Agents, Knowledge Bases & AgentCore Framework

selection_rules: Choose Amazon Bedrock for serverless, unified API access to leading foundation models without managing GPU infrastructure.
Choose Amazon SageMaker when complete control over container environments, distributed training, and custom model weights is required.
Use AWS Inferentia for cost-effective, high-throughput deep learning inference; use AWS Trainium for cost-optimized training.
common_confusions: Managing EC2 GPU clusters when serverless Bedrock models satisfy the application requirements.
Confusing SageMaker JumpStart pre-built models with fully managed Amazon Bedrock API consumption.
Overlooking AWS custom silicon (Inferentia/Trainium) in favor of standard GPUs for cost optimization.

tasks.name: Describe design considerations for applications that use foundation models (FMs).

topics.name: Criteria: Cost, Modality, Latency, Context Window & Prompt Caching
Inference Controls: Temperature, Top-P, Top-K & Stop Sequences
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) & Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Vector Databases: OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora pgvector, Neptune
Customization Spectrum: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Pre-training

selection_rules: Adopt RAG when external knowledge changes frequently or domain documents must remain private without retraining model weights.
Reserve fine-tuning for teaching specialized terminology, style, or task formats; use RAG for factual recall.
Store and query vector embeddings in Amazon OpenSearch Service or Aurora PostgreSQL (pgvector) for semantic retrieval.
common_confusions: Attempting to update model knowledge bases by fine-tuning instead of using RAG.
Confusing temperature (randomness) with top-p (nucleus sampling cumulative probability).
Believing embeddings contain human-readable text rather than high-dimensional mathematical representations.

tasks.name: Choose effective prompt engineering techniques.

topics.name: Prompting Techniques: Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought
System Prompts, Context, Instructions, Negative Prompts
Prompt Vulnerabilities: Injection, Hijacking, Jailbreaking & Leaks
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management & Versioning

selection_rules: Use Few-Shot prompting to demonstrate desired output format and constraints before attempting complex fine-tuning.
Apply Chain-of-Thought prompting for multi-step logical reasoning and mathematical calculations.
Implement prompt versioning and parameter testing using Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management.
common_confusions: Confusing zero-shot prompting with few-shot prompting.
Assuming prompt engineering eliminates the need for output validation guardrails.
Failing to protect system prompts against user prompt injection.

tasks.name: Describe the training and fine-tuning process for FMs.

topics.name: Pre-training, Instruction Tuning, Domain Adaptation & Distillation
Data Preparation: Curation, Labeling, Tokenization & Quality
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) & Direct Preference

selection_rules: Curate clean, balanced, representative prompt-response pairs when preparing instruction-tuning datasets.
Apply model distillation to transfer reasoning capabilities from a large teacher model to a lightweight student model for lower latency.
Ensure training data adheres to strict privacy and licensing boundaries before initiating fine-tuning.
common_confusions: Thinking fine-tuning requires millions of documents like pre-training; effective instruction tuning can use hundreds or thousands of high-quality examples.
Confusing model distillation (compressing model size) with quantization.
Overfitting fine-tuned models on narrow datasets, causing catastrophic forgetting of general reasoning.

tasks.name: Describe methods to evaluate FM performance.

topics.name: Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation vs Automated Benchmarks
NLP Metrics: ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore & LLM-as-a-Judge
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation Jobs & Custom Metrics
Application Metrics: RAG Precision/Recall, Task Completion & Latency

selection_rules: Use automated metrics (ROUGE for summarization, BLEU for translation) for rapid continuous benchmarking, supplemented by human review for nuance.
Utilize Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation to systematically compare model outputs across multiple foundation models with standardized prompt datasets.
Track task completion rate and cost per interaction to measure business value alongside technical metrics.
common_confusions: Relying strictly on BLEU/ROUGE for creative or conversational quality evaluation.
Evaluating model accuracy in isolation without measuring end-to-end RAG retrieval recall and precision.
Confusing benchmark performance (e.g. MMLU) with real-world enterprise workflow efficacy.

tasks.name: Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible.

topics.name: Pillars: Fairness, Inclusivity, Robustness, Safety & Veracity
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for Content Moderation & PII Redaction
Legal Risks: Copyright, IP Infringement, Bias & Trust Degradation
Dataset Bias, Demographic Parity & Representation Balance

selection_rules: Deploy Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to systematically block toxic content, deny forbidden topics, and redact PII across model inputs and outputs.
Audit training datasets for historical demographic bias before training predictive or classification models.
Implement human oversight and escalation paths for high-stakes decisions (loans, hiring, healthcare).
common_confusions: Believing foundation models automatically respect copyright or ethical guidelines without configured guardrails.
Treating bias mitigation as a one-time check rather than continuous evaluation across demographic slices.
Assuming guardrails degrade model intelligence rather than enforcing safety boundaries.

tasks.name: Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models.

topics.name: Transparent/Interpretable Models vs Black-Box Neural Networks
Amazon SageMaker Model Cards & Model Governance
Trade-offs: Accuracy vs Interpretability in Regulated Environments
Human-Centered Design: Explanations, Attribution & Feedback

selection_rules: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to document intended use, training parameters, evaluation results, and risk profiles for compliance auditability.
Select inherently interpretable models (decision trees, linear models) when regulatory compliance mandates transparent decision explanation.
Provide users with clear attribution and source citations in generative responses to foster user trust and verification.
common_confusions: Assuming complex deep neural networks offer the same post-hoc explainability as shallow models.
Neglecting model governance documentation until after production deployment.
Confusing feature importance with causal explanation.

domains.name: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

tasks.name: Explain methods to secure AI systems.

topics.name: IAM Policies, Role-Based Access & Least Privilege for Models
Data Encryption at Rest (KMS) & In Transit (TLS) for AI
VPC Endpoints & AWS PrivateLink for Amazon Bedrock
Threat Vectors: Prompt Injection, Model Inversion & Data Poisoning
Grounding Techniques & Data Lineage for Security

selection_rules: Keep model traffic private within the VPC using AWS PrivateLink VPC endpoints, avoiding public internet traversal.
Encrypt training datasets, model artifacts, and vector indices with customer-managed AWS KMS keys.
Apply input sanitization and prompt injection filters before passing user prompts to foundation models.
common_confusions: Assuming foundation model providers train public models on your private Amazon Bedrock API prompts and completions (AWS does NOT use customer data to train foundation models).
Relying on perimeter firewalls while leaving IAM permissions overly permissive.
Confusing application data encryption with vector database index security.

tasks.name: Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems.

topics.name: AWS Artifact, AWS CloudTrail & AWS Config for AI Auditing
Data Retention, Data Residency & Model Lifecycle Policies
Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix & Risk Assessment
AI Governance Frameworks, EU AI Act & Industry Compliance

selection_rules: Use AWS CloudTrail to log and monitor all API calls made to Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker for security auditing.
Consult AWS Artifact to obtain compliance reports and attestations for AI workloads in regulated industries (HIPAA, SOC, ISO).
Apply the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix to classify workloads based on model customization depth and data sensitivity.
common_confusions: Assuming third-party model providers through Bedrock have access to your AWS account credentials.
Failing to retain CloudTrail logs required for regulatory forensics and security audits.
Treating consumer-grade AI tools and enterprise-grade AWS AI services as having identical data privacy guarantees.
